'''''Helianthemum canariense''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Cistaceae]], native to [[Western Sahara]], [[Morocco]] and the [[Canary Islands]].<ref name=POWO_168783-1/>

==Description==
''Helianthemum canariense'' is a short, densely branched shrub up to {{cvt|25|cm|in|0}} tall. Its oval leaves are greyish in appearance due to a dense covering of short hairs, and are {{cvt|5|–|10|mm|in|1}} long. The pale yellow flowers are about {{cvt|1|–|2|cm|in|1}} across.<ref name=Bram01/>

<gallery mode=packed>
File:Helianthemum canariense Montana Roja.jpg|Flower
</gallery>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described by [[Nikolaus Joseph von Jacquin|Nikolaus von Jacquin]] in 1781 or 1782, as ''Cistus canariensis'', and transferred to ''[[Helianthemum]]'' in 1806 by [[Christiaan Hendrik Persoon|Christiaan Persoon]].<ref name=IPNI_168783-1/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Helianthemum canariense'' is native to the [[Canary Islands]], [[Western Sahara]] and [[Morocco]].<ref name=POWO_168783-1/> In the Canary Islands, it is found on all islands in dry areas, up to altitudes of {{cvt|600|m|ft|-2}}.<ref name=Bram01/>
